scenarios.name: Cyclone Landfall
scenarios.description: Category 3 cyclone with 165 km/h sustained winds and 3.4 m storm surge.
scenarios.narrative: Storm surge strips fringing canopy along the exposed seaward margin and breaches embankments. Interior patches survive but lose their outer buffer, isolating the seaward cluster.

scenarios.name: Urban Expansion
scenarios.description: Projected 2035 built-up footprint following the district master plan.
scenarios.narrative: Peri-urban growth consumes the landward buffer and hardens the shoreline. Corridors that once routed around settlement edges are severed, forcing longer, higher-resistance paths.

scenarios.name: Sea Level Rise
scenarios.description: IPCC SSP5-8.5 trajectory — 0.68 m mean sea level rise by 2100.
scenarios.narrative: Coastal squeeze prevents landward migration of the mangrove belt. Low-elevation mudflats drown first, removing the stepping-stone patches that currently bind the network together.

scenarios.name: Aquaculture Conversion
scenarios.description: Conversion of intertidal margin to brackish shrimp ponds.
scenarios.narrative: Pond bunding blocks tidal exchange and fragments the creek network. Hydrological isolation degrades habitat quality well beyond the converted footprint.

scenarios.name: Road / Embankment
scenarios.description: Coastal highway alignment with a raised embankment across the wetland.
scenarios.narrative: Direct habitat loss is modest, but the linear barrier bisects the landscape. Connectivity loss far exceeds area loss — the classic signature of a fragmenting infrastructure project.

scenarios.name: Illegal Encroachment
scenarios.description: Detected unauthorised clearing within the notified buffer zone.
scenarios.narrative: Scattered small clearings accumulate along accessible edges. Individually minor, collectively they erode edge integrity and open interior habitat to further incursion.
